messages:
pranav: Heads-up — I'm seeing repeated p99 latency spikes on the generation path when the paged KV gets fragmented and evicted mid-request. stack + log below.

pranav: log snippet:
```
W [2071234500]: missing page for kv_slot=4096, scheduling fetch
E kernel: fallback to generic_attn_kernel; added 120ms blocking
```

pranav: This happens on dedicated r5p pool, long-context workloads (>8k). pattern: many small KV writes -> fragmentation -> compaction kicks in -> simultaneous page fetches -> kernel falls back or stalls.

tia: thanks for surfacing. Is this reproducible in the perf harness or only in prod canaries?

pranav: Repro in harness with synthetic sparse writes + random eviction. Also saw it on canary yesterday.

alex: Quick thought: we should avoid baking page-layout semantics into the kernel. But we can add a capability contract so kernels can state what they need. e.g., "requires_contiguous_kv" vs "handles_sparse_pages". Runtime can pick appropriate kernel variant.

rachel: We experimented with zero-filled reads as a cheap fallback to avoid stalls, but it broke some generation quality (prefix-sensitive models picked wrong context). So any degraded-path needs an opt-in and per-model eval.

marcus: Another option: async page handles — kernel issues a handle for KV lookups; if handle not ready, runtime returns a placeholder and schedules a fetch. kernel can continue for other tokens. Sounds invasive but could reduce tail latency.

infra-bot: deploy: pager-2.1 -> canary (3 hosts) :heavy_check_mark:

pranav: The compaction heuristic seems to be a big contributor. It currently runs aggressively when free_pages < X. That causes many small background IO spikes. We should consider bandwidth-capped compaction or compaction backoff based on current request load.

tia: Agreed. Also need backpressure: when page-miss rate spikes, runtime should prefer sparse-tolerant kernels or shift requests to nodes with warmer caches.

alex: Interface design question — what does a capability registry look like? Proposal: kernel metadata includes a list of flags + estimated penalty for fallback. runtime has selection rules: capability superset + minimal estimated penalty.

rachel: And we need a clear compatibility shim: older kernels without flags should default to conservative selection (assume contiguous requirement). We'll add a deprecation window in the RFC.

jing: Test plan: create a suite that simulates eviction events during mid-request. two axes: fragmentation level and concurrent compaction intensity. Measure p50/p95/p99 for three kernel variants: contiguous-opt, sparse-robust, async-handle (if available).

marcus: Fallback policy matrix we discussed:
- Route to sparse kernel if available (best latency, maybe some accuracy diff)
- Serve degraded (truncate KV/pads with zeros) with a quality flag
- Block and wait for fetch (correct but highest latency)
Config per-customer and per-model.

pranav: We must also surface metrics: page_miss_rate, avg_page_fetch_ms, compaction_pause_ms, kernel_fallback_count. These drive alerts and automatic switching.

tia: Short roadmap: short-term (2 sprints) add kernel capability flags + runtime selection + metrics. Medium (next quarter) add async page-handle prototype and compaction backpressure. Long-term: refactor pager for better logical contiguity (reduce fragmentation and make kernels simpler).

alex: I'll co-own the short-term work with rachel. we'll draft a minimal API for flags and a simple selector in the runtime.

rachel: I'll write the RFC this week: include schema for kernel metadata, selection algorithm, and compatibility rules. Also sketch unit tests and perf regressions to watch.

pranav: Please include a harness test that injects eviction mid-kv-loop (like: during kv_read loop, emit eviction for target page). That caught a class of bugs earlier.

jing: I'll add the eviction-injector to the perf harness and run the three-kernel matrix. will post numbers to this thread.

marcus: Also consider an emergency mitigation: when p99 > 150ms, runtime should temporarily disable aggressive compaction or route traffic to warmer nodes.

pranav: Good call. And surface a customer-facing note for Dedicated customers about potential perf impact during compaction windows.

tia: Action items: Alex+Rachel RFC + selector impl (2 sprints), Jing adds harness tests, Marcus drafts emergency mitigation, Pranav instruments metrics. We'll sync in next architecture sync.

pranav: thanks everyone — feel better having a concrete plan. tagging @alex @rachel @jing for visibility. :rocket:
